answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must bind identities into cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs. In this architecture, registering clustered identities within an affinity grove requires staking bonds that scale exponentially across trust partitions. A single agent crossing a network ridge incurs baseline staking, but coordinating a swarm drives capital efficiency into an unviable nadir through exponential capital exhaustion, making mass spoofing mathematically cost-prohibitive.
